generated one. Other documents REFERENCE this file, or say nothing.
ONE-TRUTH-1 made 19 copies machine-written and machine-checked. That was the wrong shape: a
generated copy is still a copy, it still has to be kept in step, and a reader who finds one has
no way to know whether it is the truth or a stale rendering of it. ONE-TRUTH-2 (the owner's
order) deleted all 19. Where a document's argument needed the reader to know a fingerprint
EXISTS, it now points here; where it did not, the mention was removed.
WHERE A CURRENT VALUE MAY STILL APPEAR, and nowhere else:
- this file
- docs/TAGS.md — the tag register. A tag's hash is what it was when the tag was cut.
- reports/ — the lab journal. Append-only by rule: a report records what was true on the day
it was written and must never be rewritten. Listed as a PREFIX rather than 112 filenames,
which is a decision: enumerating them would be noise that nobody would maintain, and the
append-only rule already makes every one of them history by construction.

nothing else to update — that is the point.

camera.mintedBy:
COMPANY-HEADCOUNT-1 — THE OWNER JUDGED THE BUILD ON A PRODUCTION BUILD (59c6bb98) ON 2026-09-02 AND ACCEPTED IT, on the stated ground that he counts the racers he configured. This hash is that acceptance written down.

WHAT CHANGED. `companyGuarantee` computed `need = Math.floor(minVisible) - 1` under a comment saying the anchor itself is one of them. That was TRUE when it was written — the anchor was the subject racer's own position — and false from the moment CAMERA-LATERAL-1 replaced it with the racing-line CENTRELINE point. Measured rather than read: the anchor equals `_centrelineAt(t)` on 100% of frames and coincides with NO racer on 100% of frames, so a promise of five asked for four companions and delivered four racers, and the widening that would have shown the fifth was never requested. The state ceiling won the composition only because the state's own setting was already wider than the guarantee's understated request; nothing was restraining the shot.

THE PREMISE IS FIXED, NOT THE ARITHMETIC. The loop's existing `dx === 0 && dy === 0` test — the line that already skipped the anchor — was throwing its answer away; it is now recorded, and `need = floor(minVisible) - (anchorIsRacer ? 1 : 0)`. THE SHAPE CANNOT SILENTLY REGRESS because the premise is DERIVED per call from the same inputs the function already walks: there is no parameter, no flag and no comment asserting it, so nothing is left that can go stale when the anchor moves again. A boolean parameter would have relocated the defect to the caller — a true statement left standing while its premise moved beneath it, which is exactly what happened here.

THE SECOND CALL SITE IS CORRECT AND UNCHANGED, established by RUNNING both trees rather than by reasoning across from it. `_fieldCeiling` passes `racers.length + 1` as a sentinel meaning more than the field can supply, and the `Math.min(need, ceilings.length)` clamp turns any over-ask into take-everything — so the deduction was absorbed by that clamp and never reached the result. Probed on both trees in both anchor cases, the field site returns the identical ceiling before and after, while a promise of five with a non-racer anchor moves 1.4400 to 1.1520.

THE PRICE, ten tracks at N=30 and four at N=300, arms matched frame by frame. FRAME COUNTS ARE IDENTICAL BETWEEN ARMS ON ALL TEN TRACKS: this moves the picture and not the race. Promise kept space-sprint 96.32% to 99.23%, searound 97.39% to 99.92%, seatrack 97.55% to 99.63%, garden-path 99.59% to 100.00%. In-shot p50 is unchanged everywhere and p10 rises by one on the three worst tracks, which is the correct shape: it bites only where the promise was being broken. STEADINESS IS NOT COSTED — largest single-frame pan identical on 9 of 10 at N=30 and on all four at N=300, corner overflow unchanged or better, centreline share unchanged or better. The shot is UNTOUCHED on 82.5-98.7% of frames and where it widens it is a median 1.02-1.07x.

WHAT REMAINS, REPORTED AND NOT CLAMPED. On the frames still short at N=300 the COMPANY ceiling is itself the binding term on 77-100%, with a deficit of exactly one on 85-99%: the guarantee asking and not getting. That is consistent with the recorded defect that the anchor misses the screen point every guarantee reasons from by a median 74 px, and NOT with the headcount still being wrong. No setting was changed to absorb it.

camera.supersededMintedBy: LEADER-LATERAL-BUILD-1 — THE OWNER JUDGED THE BUILD ON A PRODUCTION BUILD (3dc061f4) ON 2026-08-26 AND ACCEPTED IT: space-sprint looks right to him. This hash is that acceptance written down. THE RULE, in his words: the camera holds the corridor centreline and steps aside laterally ONLY when the leader would otherwise be clipped, and only as far as needed; as soon as he fits from the centreline again it returns. WHY IT NEEDED MORE THAN THE OBVIOUS ONE-LINE CHANGE, measured before anything was built: adding the leader to `_applyLateralGuarantee`'s subject list changes the answer on 0 of 2,019 frames, for two independent reasons — the corridor edges are ALWAYS in that list and `lateralShiftToFit` intersects intervals, so a subject lying INSIDE them can never narrow the answer; and the corridor does not fit the frame on 100% of LEADER_ZOOM frames, which pins the helper permanently in its 'split the difference' branch, decided by the extremes alone. So the leader gets his OWN interval from the new `lateralAdmissibleForBody` — his four DRAWN BODY corners against the real frame — and the corridor's answer is CLAMPED into it; when it already keeps him whole the clamp is inert, which is 90.27% of frames. NO EASING WAS ADDED AND NONE WAS NEEDED: the rule moves the pan TARGET, and the existing first-order pan smoother is what turns a target step into a travel, so the 130.6 px 'jolt' LEADER-LATERAL-MINIMAL-1 measured never reaches the picture — a second smoother on one quantity is what this project has twice had to undo. TWO KEYS, both read off a sweep rather than chosen: `leaderLateralMarginPx` budgets for the smoother's residual trailing (without it the rule reports 'he fits' on 383 of the 394 frames that still clipped, because the promise is made at the target and broken before it is drawn — the same job `innerFramePct` does for every other subject), and `leaderLateralMaxPx` bounds the step: identical to unbounded on all four affected tracks, yet load-bearing, because a frame-rectangle test once drove this mechanism 500 world px off the centreline chasing a loss no sideways move could reach. Past the bound he stays PARTLY CLIPPED, deliberately — partial clipping is the lesser evil against a camera that swings. MEASURED, 10 tracks x 10 races per arm, 140,740 LEADER_ZOOM mid-race frames each: clip rate 4.18% -> 1.29% pooled (space-sprint 15.4% -> 3.3%, seatrack 6.5% -> 2.2%, river-run 4.6% -> 0.3%, mountainstreet 4.4% -> 0.8%); the six calm tracks are unchanged because their clipping was never sideways. THE PICTURE DID NOT MOVE: 93 of 100 races carry a >=120 px single-frame movement in BOTH arms, and the largest median change anywhere is 10.07 -> 10.15 px. STILL OPEN and deliberately not in this piece: the along-track residual (830 frames, unchanged by design — it belongs to the ZOOM guarantee, not the pan), and the corridor measuring its own room from `anchorScreenPoint` while `resolveCamera` centres the target, a median 132 px apart.
